items.About:
I work at the intersection of critical minerals, technology, investment, and workforce development, with a focus on one question: how do we move critical minerals from waste streams into the supply chain faster?

I am CEO and Co-Founder of Peblink Inc. and CMX, the Critical Minerals Exchange. CMX is focused on streamlining the path from identifying critical minerals in secondary and waste sources to recovery and commercialization.

Across mining and oil & gas, significant mineral resources exist in tailings, produced water, brines, solids, legacy mine waste, and other secondary streams. CMX brings together the science, technology, industry, investment, and workforce needed to move promising opportunities forward.

A major part of our work is de-risking early-stage opportunities so they can attract capital and advance toward commercial recovery. We connect early investors with promising projects, bring in independent scientific expertise, engage recovery technology companies, and help create a clearer pathway for larger investment as projects advance.

The goal is efficiency and speed—getting promising resources evaluated, getting private capital involved earlier, helping recovery technologies reach the right sites, and ultimately getting more critical minerals into the supply chain.

Workforce development is also a major part of CMX. We support critical mineral startups by building multidisciplinary university teams around what each company actually needs to move forward. That support can include business plans, pitch decks, market analysis, supply chain strategy, commercialization planning, environmental dashboards, data analytics, AI, computer science, cybersecurity, and marketing. We can build the team around the needs of the startup, giving emerging companies access to high-level talent and practical support as they move toward commercialization and scale.

Peblink is a global workforce development and technology company. We specialize in building university-industry partnerships and data and intelligence dashboards across critical minerals, mining, oil & gas, healthcare, and other sectors. Our projects have extended across the United States, Africa, South America, and the Middle East, working with universities, government ministries, industry, and other stakeholders to address real-world challenges.

Across all of this work, my focus is consistent: connecting science, technology, capital, industry, and talent to move strong ideas into real-world faster.

patents.title: Methods and systems for vehicle-based tracking of nearby events
patents.description: The present disclosure generally relates to methods, systems, apparatuses, and non-transitory computer readable media for incident detection using radar sensory data. A vehicular tracking system comprises at least one on-vehicle sensor, such as a radar sensor, that can perceive the environment around the vehicle and capture data related to possible incidents that may be viewed by the sensor. A radar sensor may provide radar data that can be used to calculate velocity vectors, accelerations vectors, azimuth and elevation angles of other vehicles, and this data may be collected and stored for possible incident characterization and accident investigation. The vehicle with the sensor may be configured to behave as a third-party witness to possible incidents. Several sensors may be used in conjunction with one another, where one sensor may trigger another sensor to begin capturing other data that the first sensor may be unable to capture.

raw_items.headline: CEO/Co-Founder. Peblink and World Literacy Research Center. Project management in critical mineral recovery from waste.
raw_items.about:
I work at the intersection of critical minerals, technology, investment, and workforce development, with a focus on one question: how do we move critical minerals from waste streams into the supply chain faster?

I am CEO and Co-Founder of Peblink Inc. and CMX, the Critical Minerals Exchange. CMX is focused on streamlining the path from identifying critical minerals in secondary and waste sources to recovery and commercialization.

Across mining and oil & gas, significant mineral resources exist in tailings, produced water, brines, solids, legacy mine waste, and other secondary streams. CMX brings together the science, technology, industry, investment, and workforce needed to move promising opportunities forward.

A major part of our work is de-risking early-stage opportunities so they can attract capital and advance toward commercial recovery. We connect early investors with promising projects, bring in independent scientific expertise, engage recovery technology companies, and help create a clearer pathway for larger investment as projects advance.

The goal is efficiency and speed—getting promising resources evaluated, getting private capital involved earlier, helping recovery technologies reach the right sites, and ultimately getting more critical minerals into the supply chain.

Workforce development is also a major part of CMX. We support critical mineral startups by building multidisciplinary university teams around what each company actually needs to move forward. That support can include business plans, pitch decks, market analysis, supply chain strategy, commercialization planning, environmental dashboards, data analytics, AI, computer science, cybersecurity, and marketing. We can build the team around the needs of the startup, giving emerging companies access to high-level talent and practical support as they move toward commercialization and scale.

Peblink is a global workforce development and technology company. We specialize in building university-industry partnerships and data and intelligence dashboards across critical minerals, mining, oil & gas, healthcare, and other sectors. Our projects have extended across the United States, Africa, South America, and the Middle East, working with universities, government ministries, industry, and other stakeholders to address real-world challenges.

Across all of this work, my focus is consistent: connecting science, technology, capital, industry, and talent to move strong ideas into real-world faster.

raw_items.headline: Co-Founder @ CoffeeSpace | Matching cofounders & early startup hires | StartX S25 | Ex-World Bank & MIT
raw_items.about:
I live and breathe being a connector. Whether it’s connecting people to people, people to opportunities, or capital to promising ideas, I love it all. 

It’s a passion I’ve carried throughout my journey with the World Bank, MIT, and as an investor. And it’s also why I'm building CoffeeSpace, the infrastructure for early-stage team formation — starting with an AI-powered platform that connects founders to cofounders and early hires through high-signal matching.

When I’m not working, you’ll likely find me at the gym, analyzing markets, or crafting a new Magic: The Gathering deck. I’m also a proud Coldplay fan – ‘Paradise’ and ‘Clocks’ are on constant repeat in my playlist (and probably outplay my next 20 favorite songs combined).

currentPosition.description:

Since launch, we’ve grown to 30,000+ users, facilitating 2.5M+ swipes and 65,000+ matches.
 
Selected for TechCrunch Disrupt 2024’s Startup Battlefield 200, ranked Top 5 Product of the Day on Product Hunt, featured in Forbes, TechCrunch, and Tech in Asia, and part of the StartX S25 cohort.
 
To date, we’ve raised $1M from exited founders, YC alumni, and execs from Meta, Google, Stripe, Sand Hill Angels, and more.

raw_items.headline: Enterprise & Public Sector Sales | GTM Strategy | Cybersecurity & AI
raw_items.about: I've made a living reading rooms: security audits, poker tables, the White House complex, and the other side of a negotiation. I started out auditing other people's security programs, which mostly meant telling companies what was broken. Eventually my boss and I decided we could do it better ourselves, so we left and built the firm. He delivered, I sold, and every dollar that came through the door came through me. I spent a couple of years after that playing poker professionally. Then I joined the Secret Service and spent three years at the White House complex recalibrating what counts as a high-stakes meeting. I came back to revenue in federal, carried a growth number, and more recently built go-to-market from zero for an AI startup. The pattern holds: I show up where the pipeline doesn't exist and build one. Enterprise and public sector, cybersecurity and AI.

currentPosition.description: I drive the growth of Google’s cybersecurity business by building strategic relationships and delivering advanced security solutions across Federal Civilian accounts. Advisory practice serving founders and executive teams on go-to-market and revenue strategy, alongside a one-to-one executive coaching line.

Advisory engagements have included building go-to-market from zero for an AI startup: multi-vertical pipeline, account plans, value narratives, and pricing, plus leading a cross-functional pursuit through investor diligence to a signed private equity letter of intent and closing partnerships with a leading academic medical center and national organizations.

On the coaching side, full-cycle seller: generated demand, ran discovery, and closed engagements with founders and C-suite operators, built on a paid acquisition system producing qualified leads.
Advised the CEO on company strategy and direction, supported private equity fundraising, and helped close new customer deals and onboard vendor partners to the platform.

Owned customer growth on a task order within a U.S. Government IDIQ, carrying a 12% annual expansion target and delivering 100% of quota. Grew scope inside an existing federal account by surfacing new requirements and converting them into funded work. Defended the account through recompete across program office, contracting officers, and technical evaluators.

Served the protective mission at the White House complex, including the West Wing, operating daily in proximity to the President, cabinet officials, and visiting heads of state. Executed under continuous scrutiny in an environment with no margin for error, coordinating across federal agencies, military components, and outside law enforcement with no direct authority over any of them. Completed federal law enforcement training at FLETC and the Secret Service Training Center.
Built the startup's first sales and marketing team and rebuilt the go-to-market strategy and value proposition.

Bootstrapped a GRC and information security consultancy, responsible for all revenue generated as the sole closer, with no outside funding, owning prospecting, discovery, proposals, negotiation, and signature. Signed and grew the flagship enterprise account with $1M+ total contract value, negotiated directly with the CIOs of enterprise level accounts and renewed across three years. Built the book of business using assessment/pilot engagements sold to security and compliance leaders across regulated industries, leading cross-functional teams of assessors, auditors, and technical consultants to scope and win multi-stakeholder deals.

Performed GRC audits of enterprise information security programs, assessing controls against regulatory and framework requirements. Conducted risk assessments and social engineering testing, delivering findings and remediation guidance to security and compliance leadership.

Sole revenue owner, growing the company from $2M to $7M by winning and expanding contracts with national and regional insurance carriers. Negotiated per-service rate structures with carrier procurement and claims leadership, protecting margin across a nationwide network of contracted tow operators. Owned the full business: sales, call center, hiring, and management team, scaling to 70+ employees.

Working with Jason has been an absolute pleasure and one of the most rewarding professional experiences I’ve had. I had the opportunity to support him as his Sales & Operations Coordinator at Performance Through Balance, and I can genuinely say that Jason is an outstanding client and an incredible person to work with.

Jason is professional, respectful, highly driven, and incredibly intentional about the work he does. What truly sets him apart is his ability to lead with clarity, purpose, and genuine care for people. He doesn’t simply focus on getting things done. He focuses on doing things the right way and creating meaningful, sustainable results.

I’ve learned a great deal from working alongside Jason, and I’m truly grateful for the opportunity to see firsthand how much thought, purpose, and heart he puts into helping people become better versions of themselves.

Jason creates an environment where you feel trusted, valued, and empowered to contribute. He communicates clearly, provides thoughtful feedback, and has an incredible ability to bring out the best in the people around him.

If you’re considering working with Jason, I highly recommend him without hesitation. Whether as a client, coach, leader, or business partner, he brings professionalism, integrity, purpose, and excellence to everything he does.

Thank you, Jason, for the trust, guidance, and opportunity to work with you. It was truly a great pleasure, and I would be very happy to work with you again in the future.

I am happy to write this recommendation on behalf of Jason Sardo. I have known Jason since his Freshman year in college when he knocked on my office door, introduced himself and just asked if we could discuss philosophy. He was not in any of my classes at the time. Jason immediately impressed me s a person who likes to analyze and evaluate difficult arguments. His communication skills were already strong at that time, and they have improved every year since. Moreover, I have enjoyed watching Jason mature and grow, both as a person and as student. While he did struggle in some of his early courses, Jason clearly resolved that he was going to improve, and that has been exactly what he has done all the way up through graduate school. Currently, he is a leader in his graduate program, and he is one of the top students. As a teacher, Jason's story is the kind I love to tell, because through effort and persistence, Jason has truly transformed himself into a highly skilled profession who has pride of work. Finally, on a personal level, Jason is very friendly and has a good sense of humor. I recommend Jason, therefore, without reservation.

If you have any further questions, feel free to contact me at snow@hilbert.edu.

Gordon Snow Ph.D.
